summary: Embedding endpoint retry amplification causing rerank p95 latency spikes and partial result sets
description:
Issue summary:
Customer LedgerDocs reports repeated p95 latency spikes on their /v1/embeddings -> /v1/rerank workflow starting 2026-03-11 08:00 UTC. High-level symptoms: long tail (p95/p99) increases from ~350ms to >3s, intermittent partial result sets (rerank returns 3–5 candidates instead of expected 10) and elevated 5xx retries between embed proxy and serving runtime.

Impact:
- Affects a single dedicated tenant (LedgerDocs) in us-east.
- Production traffic experiences user-visible slowness and degraded retrieval quality.
- Customer SLA (dedicated throughput) risk if sustained.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated pool: ded-us-east-3
- API path: POST /v1/embeddings (redwood-embed-256) -> POST /v1/rerank
- Client traffic pattern: bursty batch of 64 embed requests followed by synchronous rerank for each batch.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Send 64 document embed requests in parallel, pin model redwood-embed-256.
2) Immediately call rerank endpoint with top_k=10 using returned embedding ids.
3) Observe p95 and returned candidate count.

Observed behavior:
- p50 unaffected; p95/p99 spikes correlate with short-lived embed proxy 502/504 and internal retries.
- Rerank responses frequently contain 3–6 candidates or return early with status 206 when upstream times out.
- Metric spike: embed_proxy.retry_rate increased x5 during incidents; router queue depth briefly spiked.
- Logs show embed-worker processes backing off and connection resets to ANN shards.

Expected behavior:
- Stable p95 under 500ms for this traffic profile and full candidate sets of 10.

Relevant logs/IDs:
- Customer request examples: req-ld-20260311-8a1f
- Observed router trace: trace-us-east-ld-20260311-07
- Metrics chart: grafana/dashboard/embed-latency?panel=7&from=2026-03-11T07:50Z

Investigation notes (initial):
- Hypothesis A: Retry amplification — embed proxy retries on transient 5xx while router also re-routes, leading to duplicate inflight work and worker starvation.
- Hypothesis B: ANN shard reclaim or GC causing temporary reduced capacity and increased latency; retries amplify the pressure.
- Correlated infra event: autoscaler reported transient inability to allocate extra serving replicas for ded-us-east-3 at 2026-03-11 07:58 UTC (see infra alert INFRA-7642).
- Trace sampling shows multiple embed requests de-duplicated at api-gateway but still forwarded to proxy due to missing idempotency token on batch calls.

Workaround applied:
- Support toggled proxy short-circuit for LedgerDocs to reduce client-side retries (disabled client-side retry header honor for 30m).
- Advised customer to enable idempotency tokens on batch embed calls; provided code snippet.
- Temporarily increased replica cap for ded-us-east-3 to reduce autoscaler pressure.

Next steps / action items:
- Engineering to add adaptive retry throttling in embed-proxy (limit bursts when embed-proxy.retry_rate rises). (Owner: Ethan)
- Add idempotency enforcement docs and example in SDKs (Owner: DevEX).
- Run replay test that mimics LedgerDocs burst pattern to ensure mitigation. (Owner: SRE)
- Follow-up: run post-incident evaluation and add to postmortem if recurrence.

Notes on customer communication:
- Customer notified of initial triage and workaround 2026-03-11 09:05 UTC.
- Will provide timeline after final root cause.
